description.value: The study investigated whether precedent descriptions presenting unpleasant pictures as fictitious rather than real scenes attenuated emotional brain responses during an emotional judgment task.

value: we hypothesized that the differential brain responses between unpleasant and neutral pictures would be attenuated (or even eliminated) in the fictitious condition compared to the real condition.
we predicted that the activity of amygdala and insula to highly arousing unpleasant images would be flexible and adaptive in the context of an extrinsic and incidental reappraisal strategy.

spans.text: Thus, we hypothesized that the differential brain responses between unpleasant and neutral pictures would be attenuated (or even eliminated) in the fictitious condition compared to the real condition. Particularly, we predicted that the activity of amygdala and insula to highly arousing unpleasant images would be flexible and adaptive in the context of an extrinsic and incidental reappraisal strategy.

description.value: The experiment used a 2 (context: fictitious and real) × 2 (valence: neutral and unpleasant) factorial design. Twenty-two healthy volunteers completed one experimental session comprising four counterbalanced runs.

value: removal of first three functional volumes

spans.text: The first three functional volumes of each run were removed to eliminate non-equilibrium magnetization effects. The remaining images were corrected for head movement by realigning all the images to the first image via rigid body transformations. The images were then corrected for differences in slice acquisition time. For each participant, functional and structural images were co-registered. Structural data were normalized by matching them to the standardized MNI template, and the transformation parameters estimated in this step were applied to all functional images. Functional images were spatially smoothed with an 8-mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel prior to statistical analysis.

Data quality and motion/artifact effects were checked and corrected using Artifact Repair version 4.

model_settings.value: Two-stage mixed-effects analysis. At first level, regressors for neutral and unpleasant pictures in real and fictitious contexts were convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function and entered into a multiple-regression general linear model. At second level, group Student t-tests were performed. A voxelwise threshold of P=0.001 uncorrected and a minimum cluster size of 10 contiguous voxels were used.
